title: Overview
content:
Good Boy is a 2025 American horror film written and directed by Ben Leonberg. The film is produced by IFC Films and is distinguished by being told entirely from the point of view of a dog investigating a haunted house. The canine protagonist, portrayed by a dog named Indy/Indie, experiences and responds to supernatural phenomena while his human family explores a ghost-infested property. [1][2][3][4][5][6][8][9][10][11][12][14][16][17][19]

Good Boy premiered at the 2025 South by Southwest (SXSW) Film & TV Festival before receiving a wider theatrical release. IFC Films acquired and distributed the film, ultimately giving it a wide release in the United States on 3 October 2025 following significant online interest in the trailer. The film has attracted attention from trade publications and genre outlets for its formally unusual dog point-of-view concept and its blend of haunted house horror with offbeat humor. [1][2][3][4][5][6][8][9][10][11][12][14][16][17][19]

title: Documented conflicts and limitations
content:
Several publicly available sources about Good Boy present minor discrepancies or leave certain production details only partially documented. [1][2][3][4][5][6][8][10][11][14][16][18][19][20][21]

One documented conflict concerns the films runtime. IndieWire reports the running time as 72 minutes, while the Gateway Film Centers cinema listing gives a runtime of 73 minutes. Neither source offers an explanation for the one-minute difference, such as distinguishing between festival and theatrical cuts, and no official clarification is provided in the materials consulted. [1][2][3][4][5][6][8][10][11][14][16][18][19][20][21]

Sources also diverge on how they credit the films cinematography. Some database entries and credit listings name Wade Grebnoel as the director of photography, with contextual information suggesting that this is a pseudonym associated with Ben Leonberg, whereas other listings simply credit Wade Grebnoel without any indication that the name functions as an alias. As a result, the exact relationship between Leonberg and the credited cinematographer cannot be conclusively established on the basis of the available sources. [1][2][3][4][5][6][8][10][11][14][16][18][19][20][21]

There is a spelling inconsistency in references to the dog performer, who is variously named 
Indy
 and 
Indie
 in different materials. While both sources clearly refer to the same canine actor, no definitive official spelling is established across all promotional and reference documents. Relatedly, one director profile describes Good Boy as having been made by a three-person team over the course of three years, emphasizing the compact nature of the core creative group, whereas public credit listings such as those found on film databases and catalogues list a larger number of crew members. This suggests that the 
crew of three
